To be more precise: `<ul>` has a default margin of 10px bottom in bootstrap. It's not an issue if you precisely follow the bootstrap DOM format but otherwise it does not works.

So `<div>` being unstyled by default will in the end by easier to use for most websites.

Example:

![2015-09-09-100326_293x158_scrot](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/123822/9756387/0dfc1b7c-56da-11e5-841a-4f59eb16a366.png)

comments.body: 2 commits are hijacking this PR I think :)
Yes my PR command line tool (npm install -g gh) use the latest commit msg as PR title
Would make sense to rename the PR then ;)

This really looks like an issue with Bootstrap CSS, and should be fixed with CSS, not by editing our widgets. We chose Bootstrap because it was easy to use for our demo, but this should not have any influence on how we build our widgets.

> So `<div>` being unstyled by default will in the end by easier to use for most websites.

Don't think so. The easier for most websites will be to style a list like they already style lists. They could reuse the styles they have for `ul`/`li` and this will just work™. I even think most of them will already have a search page with a list of refinements (handled server-side) which will be rendered using `ul`/`li`.

> Don't think so. The easier for most websites will be to style a list like they already style lists. They could reuse the styles they have for ul/li and this will just work™. I even think most of them will already have a search page with a list of refinements (handled server-side) which will be rendered using ul/li.

:8ball: here! I will be happy to discover the opposite when we go further and do the needed work to put back `<ul><li>`.

Right, I have no data on this point. We'll see when the time comes.

Nevertheless, my first point still holds. If we provide a list of elements, we should use the correct markup for it. As a user, I expect plugins to generate correct markup, one that I could easily style. And having semantic markup is way better than `div`.
